sanskrit.deva:
तदेतत्सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा सन्ततानि ।
तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad etat satyaṃ mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayo yāny apaśyaṃs tāni tretāyāṃ bahudhā santatāni |
tāny ācaratha niyataṃ satyakāmā eṣa vaḥ panthāḥ sukṛtasya loke || 1 ||

lines.iast: tad etat satyaṃ mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayo yāny apaśyaṃs tāni tretāyāṃ bahudhā santatāni
lines.deva: तदेतत्सत्यं मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयो यान्यपश्यंस्तानि त्रेतायां बहुधा सन्ततानि

lines.iast: tāny ācaratha niyataṃ satyakāmā eṣa vaḥ panthāḥ sukṛtasya loke
lines.deva: तान्याचरथ नियतं सत्यकामा एष वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके

padaccheda.iast: tat etat satyam mantreṣu karmāṇi kavayaḥ yāni apaśyan tāni tretāyām bahudhā santatāni tāni ācaratha niyatam satya-kāmāḥ eṣaḥ vaḥ panthāḥ sukṛtasya loke
padaccheda.deva: तत् एतत् सत्यम् मन्त्रेषु कर्माणि कवयः यानि अपश्यन् तानि त्रेतायाम् बहुधा सन्ततानि तानि आचरथ नियतम् सत्य-कामाः एषः वः पन्थाः सुकृतस्य लोके

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. pl.

translations.text: This is the truth: the rites which the seers saw in the mantras are spread out in many ways in the triad (of the Vedas). Perform them constantly, desiring their true (fruit); this is your path to the world (the fruit) of what you have yourselves done well.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the khaṇḍa: the lower knowledge, the Vedas with their limbs, has been named (1.1.5), and the higher, by which the imperishable is attained, has been described (1.1.6–9). Now the objects of the two are to be told apart: the round of birth and death and liberation. The round, the object of the lower knowledge, made of the differences of agent, means, act and fruit, is without beginning or end, sorrow by nature, to be left by each embodied being, an unbroken stream like a river; its stilling, liberation, the object of the higher, is without beginning or end, ageless, deathless, immortal, fearless, pure, clear, resting in itself, the supreme bliss, without a second. The object of the lower knowledge is shown first, for only when it is seen can dispassion toward it arise; so the Upaniṣad will say ‘having examined the worlds built up by action’ (1.2.12), and there is no examining what has not been shown.

Śaṅkara: satyam: not false, being a sure means to the human end. The rites, the agnihotra and the rest, were made known by the mantras themselves, the Ṛgveda and the others, and the wise seers, Vasiṣṭha and the rest, saw them. tretāyām: in the triad of the Vedas, as the duties of the hotṛ, the adhvaryu and the udgātṛ; or mostly in the Tretā age. satyakāmāḥ: desiring the fruit of rites as it truly is. sukṛta: the rite one has done oneself; its loka, what is seen and enjoyed, is its fruit; this is the sure means to that fruit.

sanskrit.deva:
यदा लेलायते ह्यर्चिः समिद्धे हव्यवाहने ।
तदाज्यभागावन्तरेणाहुतीः प्रतिपादयेत् ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
yadā lelāyate hy arciḥ samiddhe havyavāhane |
tadājyabhāgāv antareṇāhutīḥ pratipādayet || 2 ||

lines.iast: yadā lelāyate hy arciḥ samiddhe havyavāhane
lines.deva: यदा लेलायते ह्यर्चिः समिद्धे हव्यवाहने

lines.iast: tadājyabhāgāv antareṇāhutīḥ pratipādayet
lines.deva: तदाज्यभागावन्तरेणाहुतीः प्रतिपादयेत्

padaccheda.iast: yadā lelāyate hi arciḥ samiddhe havya-vāhane tadā ājya-bhāgau antareṇa āhutīḥ pratipādayet
padaccheda.deva: यदा लेलायते हि अर्चिः समिद्धे हव्य-वाहने तदा आज्य-भागौ अन्तरेण आहुतीः प्रतिपादयेत्

grammar.en: past passive participle m. loc. sg.

translations.text: When the flame flickers in the kindled fire, the bearer of offerings, then one should offer the oblations between the two portions of ghee.

notes: Śaṅkara: the agnihotra is named first as the example, being the first of all rites. When the fire is well kindled with fuel laid on and the flame moves, one should cast the oblations, for the deity, between the two portions of ghee, at the place of casting. The plural ‘oblations’ is said with a view to performance on many days. This way of rites, the right casting of oblations and the rest, is the path to gain the worlds; but doing it rightly is hard, and the failings are many.

sanskrit.iast:
yasyāgnihotram adarśam apaurṇamāsam acāturmāsyam anāgrayaṇam atithivarjitaṃ ca |
ahutam avaiśvadevam avidhinā hutam āsaptamāṃs tasya lokān hinasti || 3 ||

lines.iast: yasyāgnihotram adarśam apaurṇamāsam acāturmāsyam anāgrayaṇam atithivarjitaṃ ca
lines.deva: यस्याग्निहोत्रमदर्शमपौर्णमासमचातुर्मास्यमनाग्रयणमतिथिवर्जितं च

lines.iast: ahutam avaiśvadevam avidhinā hutam āsaptamāṃs tasya lokān hinasti
lines.deva: अहुतमवैश्वदेवमविधिना हुतमासप्तमांस्तस्य लोकान्हिनस्ति

padaccheda.iast: yasya agnihotram adarśam apaurṇamāsam acāturmāsyam anāgrayaṇam atithi-varjitam ca ahutam avaiśvadevam avidhinā hutam āsaptamān tasya lokān hinasti
padaccheda.deva: यस्य अग्निहोत्रम् अदर्शम् अपौर्णमासम् अचातुर्मास्यम् अनाग्रयणम् अतिथि-वर्जितम् च अहुतम् अवैश्वदेवम् अविधिना हुतम् आसप्तमान् तस्य लोकान् हिनस्ति

words.meaning: without the offering to all the gods

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: He whose agnihotra is without the new-moon and the full-moon rites, without the four-monthly rites and the first-fruits rite, without (the honouring of) guests, not offered (at its time), without the offering to all the gods, or offered against the rule: (such a rite) destroys his worlds up to the seventh.

notes: Śaṅkara: these words describe the agnihotra, since the new-moon rite and the rest must be done by one who keeps the agnihotra and belong to it. āgrayaṇa: the rite of first fruits, done in autumn and other seasons. atithivarjita: when guests are not honoured day by day. ahutam: not offered by himself at the right time. hinasti: destroys, as it were, for its fruit is only toil. Rites rightly done win as their fruit the seven worlds, bhūḥ up to satya, according to the working out of the rite; a rite so badly done cannot win them, so they are as if destroyed, and toil alone is sure. Or the seven worlds are father, grandfather, great-grandfather, son, grandson, great-grandson and oneself, who help one another by the offering of rice-balls and the like; such a rite does not win them.

sanskrit.deva:
काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा ।
स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā |
sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ || 4 ||

lines.iast: kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā
lines.deva: काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा

lines.iast: sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānā iti sapta jihvāḥ
lines.deva: स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमाना इति सप्त जिह्वाः

padaccheda.iast: kālī karālī ca manojavā ca sulohitā yā ca sudhūmravarṇā sphuliṅginī viśvarucī ca devī lelāyamānāḥ iti sapta jihvāḥ
padaccheda.deva: काली कराली च मनोजवा च सुलोहिता या च सुधूम्रवर्णा स्फुलिङ्गिनी विश्वरुची च देवी लेलायमानाः इति सप्त जिह्वाः

translations.text: Kālī, Karālī, Manojavā, Sulohitā, Sudhūmravarṇā, Sphuliṅginī and the goddess Viśvarucī: these are the seven flickering tongues (of fire).

notes: Śaṅkara: these seven, from Kālī to Viśvarucī, are the flickering tongues of fire, there to swallow the oblations of offering.

sanskrit.deva:
एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं चाहुतयो ह्याददायन् ।
तं नयन्त्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
eteṣu yaś carate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālaṃ cāhutayo hy ādadāyan |
taṃ nayanty etāḥ sūryasya raśmayo yatra devānāṃ patir eko 'dhivāsaḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: eteṣu yaś carate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālaṃ cāhutayo hy ādadāyan
lines.deva: एतेषु यश्चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालं चाहुतयो ह्याददायन्

lines.iast: taṃ nayanty etāḥ sūryasya raśmayo yatra devānāṃ patir eko 'dhivāsaḥ
lines.deva: तं नयन्त्येताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयो यत्र देवानां पतिरेकोऽधिवासः

padaccheda.iast: eteṣu yaḥ carate bhrājamāneṣu yathākālam ca āhutayaḥ hi ādadāyan tam nayanti etāḥ sūryasya raśmayaḥ yatra devānām patiḥ ekaḥ adhivāsaḥ
padaccheda.deva: एतेषु यः चरते भ्राजमानेषु यथाकालम् च आहुतयः हि आददायन् तम् नयन्ति एताः सूर्यस्य रश्मयः यत्र देवानाम् पतिः एकः अधिवासः

translations.text: He who performs (the rites) at the proper time in these shining (tongues): these oblations take him and, as the rays of the sun, lead him to where the one lord of the gods dwells above all.

notes: Śaṅkara: eteṣu: in these different tongues of fire, as they blaze, the one who keeps the agnihotra performs his rites, without letting the time of each pass. The oblations he has made take the sacrificer and lead him, becoming the rays of the sun, that is, by the doors of the rays, to heaven, where the lord of the gods, Indra, dwells alone above all.

sanskrit.deva:
एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहन्ति ।
प्रियां वाचमभिवदन्त्योऽर्चयन्त्य एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ehy ehīti tam āhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ sūryasya raśmibhir yajamānaṃ vahanti |
priyāṃ vācam abhivadantyo 'rcayantya eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmalokaḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: ehy ehīti tam āhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ sūryasya raśmibhir yajamānaṃ vahanti
lines.deva: एह्येहीति तमाहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिर्यजमानं वहन्ति

lines.iast: priyāṃ vācam abhivadantyo 'rcayantya eṣa vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛto brahmalokaḥ
lines.deva: प्रियां वाचमभिवदन्त्योऽर्चयन्त्य एष वः पुण्यः सुकृतो ब्रह्मलोकः

padaccheda.iast: ehi ehi iti tam āhutayaḥ suvarcasaḥ sūryasya raśmibhiḥ yajamānam vahanti priyām vācam abhivadantyaḥ arcayantyaḥ eṣaḥ vaḥ puṇyaḥ sukṛtaḥ brahma-lokaḥ
padaccheda.deva: एहि एहि इति तम् आहुतयः सुवर्चसः सूर्यस्य रश्मिभिः यजमानम् वहन्ति प्रियाम् वाचम् अभिवदन्त्यः अर्चयन्त्यः एषः वः पुण्यः सुकृतः ब्रह्म-लोकः

translations.text: ‘Come, come!’ (they say), and the radiant oblations carry the sacrificer by the rays of the sun, speaking pleasing words and honouring him: ‘This is your holy world of Brahmā (heaven), won by your good deeds.’

notes: Śaṅkara: how they carry him by the sun's rays: calling him ‘come, come’, the bright oblations speak pleasing words, praise and the like, and honour him, saying ‘this is your holy world, the fruit of your good deeds’. brahmaloka: heaven, from the context.

sanskrit.deva:
प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपा अष्टादशोक्तमवरं येषु कर्म ।
एतच्छ्रेयो येऽभिनन्दन्ति मूढा जरामृत्युं ते पुनरेवापि यन्ति ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ yeṣu karma |
etac chreyo ye 'bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punar evāpi yanti || 7 ||

lines.iast: plavā hy ete adṛḍhā yajñarūpā aṣṭādaśoktam avaraṃ yeṣu karma
lines.deva: प्लवा ह्येते अदृढा यज्ञरूपा अष्टादशोक्तमवरं येषु कर्म

lines.iast: etac chreyo ye 'bhinandanti mūḍhā jarāmṛtyuṃ te punar evāpi yanti
lines.deva: एतच्छ्रेयो येऽभिनन्दन्ति मूढा जरामृत्युं ते पुनरेवापि यन्ति

padaccheda.iast: plavāḥ hi ete adṛḍhāḥ yajña-rūpāḥ aṣṭādaśa uktam avaram yeṣu karma etat śreyaḥ ye abhinandanti mūḍhāḥ jarā-mṛtyum te punaḥ eva api yanti
padaccheda.deva: प्लवाः हि एते अदृढाः यज्ञ-रूपाः अष्टादश उक्तम् अवरम् येषु कर्म एतत् श्रेयः ये अभिनन्दन्ति मूढाः जरा-मृत्युम् ते पुनः एव अपि यन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Passing, unsteady, are these forms of sacrifice, the eighteen on whom, it is said, the lower rite rests. The deluded who delight in this as the good go again to old age and death.

notes: Śaṅkara: rites without knowledge, whose fruit is only so much, the effect of ignorance, desire and action, are without substance and the root of sorrow; so they are now censured. plavāḥ: perishing. yajñarūpāḥ: those who make up the sacrifice: the sixteen priests, the wife and the sacrificer, eighteen. The rite resting on them, mere rite without knowledge, is called the lower. Since the eighteen are unsteady, the rite they accomplish passes away together with its fruit, as milk and curd are lost when the pot breaks. The undiscerning who rejoice in it as the means to the good stay a while in heaven and then go again to old age and death.

sanskrit.deva:
अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः ।
जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃmanyamānāḥ |
jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ || 8 ||

lines.iast: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayaṃ dhīrāḥ paṇḍitaṃmanyamānāḥ
lines.deva: अविद्यायामन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयं धीराः पण्डितंमन्यमानाः

lines.iast: jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhā andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ
lines.deva: जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढा अन्धेनैव नीयमाना यथान्धाः

padaccheda.iast: avidyāyām antare vartamānāḥ svayam dhīrāḥ paṇḍitam-manyamānāḥ jaṅghanyamānāḥ pariyanti mūḍhāḥ andhena eva nīyamānāḥ yathā andhāḥ
padaccheda.deva: अविद्यायाम् अन्तरे वर्तमानाः स्वयम् धीराः पण्डितम्-मन्यमानाः जङ्घन्यमानाः परियन्ति मूढाः अन्धेन एव नीयमानाः यथा अन्धाः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Living in the midst of ignorance, wise in their own eyes, thinking themselves learned, the deluded go round and round, sorely beaten, like the blind led by one who is blind.

notes: Śaṅkara: living in ignorance, mostly without discernment, they think ‘we alone are wise, learned, we know what is to be known’. jaṅghanyamānāḥ: struck again and again, sorely afflicted by old age, disease and a host of other ills, they wander about; having no sight, they are like the blind who, led by a blind man, fall into pits and thorns.

sanskrit.deva:
अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमाना वयं कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यन्ति बालाः ।
यत्कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयन्ति रागात्तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्च्यवन्ते ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
avidyāyāṃ bahudhā vartamānā vayaṃ kṛtārthā ity abhimanyanti bālāḥ |
yat karmiṇo na pravedayanti rāgāt tenāturāḥ kṣīṇalokāś cyavante || 9 ||

lines.iast: avidyāyāṃ bahudhā vartamānā vayaṃ kṛtārthā ity abhimanyanti bālāḥ
lines.deva: अविद्यायां बहुधा वर्तमाना वयं कृतार्था इत्यभिमन्यन्ति बालाः

lines.iast: yat karmiṇo na pravedayanti rāgāt tenāturāḥ kṣīṇalokāś cyavante
lines.deva: यत्कर्मिणो न प्रवेदयन्ति रागात्तेनातुराः क्षीणलोकाश्च्यवन्ते

padaccheda.iast: avidyāyām bahudhā vartamānāḥ vayam kṛtārthāḥ iti abhimanyanti bālāḥ yat karmiṇaḥ na pravedayanti rāgāt tena āturāḥ kṣīṇa-lokāḥ cyavante
padaccheda.deva: अविद्यायाम् बहुधा वर्तमानाः वयम् कृतार्थाः इति अभिमन्यन्ति बालाः यत् कर्मिणः न प्रवेदयन्ति रागात् तेन आतुराः क्षीण-लोकाः च्यवन्ते

translations.text: Living in ignorance in many ways, the childish think, ‘We have reached our goal.’ Because the men of rites do not know (the truth), from attachment (to the fruit), they fall, stricken, when their worlds are exhausted.

notes: Śaṅkara: bālāḥ: the ignorant. They do not know the truth because they are overcome by attachment to the fruit of rites; therefore, pained by sorrow, when the fruit of their rites is spent they fall from the world of heaven.

sanskrit.deva:
इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः ।
नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं लोकं हीनतरं वा विशन्ति ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
iṣṭāpūrtaṃ manyamānā variṣṭhaṃ nānyac chreyo vedayante pramūḍhāḥ |
nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte 'nubhūtvemaṃ lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśanti || 10 ||

lines.iast: iṣṭāpūrtaṃ manyamānā variṣṭhaṃ nānyac chreyo vedayante pramūḍhāḥ
lines.deva: इष्टापूर्तं मन्यमाना वरिष्ठं नान्यच्छ्रेयो वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः

lines.iast: nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte 'nubhūtvemaṃ lokaṃ hīnataraṃ vā viśanti
lines.deva: नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृतेऽनुभूत्वेमं लोकं हीनतरं वा विशन्ति

padaccheda.iast: iṣṭāpūrtam manyamānāḥ variṣṭham na anyat śreyaḥ vedayante pramūḍhāḥ nākasya pṛṣṭhe te sukṛte anubhūtvā imam lokam hīnataram vā viśanti
padaccheda.deva: इष्टापूर्तम् मन्यमानाः वरिष्ठम् न अन्यत् श्रेयः वेदयन्ते प्रमूढाः नाकस्य पृष्ठे ते सुकृते अनुभूत्वा इमम् लोकम् हीनतरम् वा विशन्ति

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

words.meaning: in the place of their good deeds

translations.text: Thinking sacrifices and works of merit the best, the utterly deluded know no other good. Having enjoyed (the fruit) on the height of heaven, in the place of their good deeds, they enter this world or a lower one.

notes: Śaṅkara: iṣṭa: sacrifice and the other rites of the Veda; pūrta: works taught in the law books, wells, tanks, reservoirs. They think these the chief means to the human end, and do not know the other means to the good, the knowledge of the Self; pramūḍhāḥ: deluded by heedless attachment to sons, cattle and kin. sukṛte: in the place where enjoyment is had. Having enjoyed the fruit of their rites there, they enter this human world, or a lower one, as animals or in hell, according to what is left of their action.

sanskrit.deva:
तपःश्रद्धे ये ह्युपवसन्त्यरण्ये शान्ता विद्वांसो भैक्षचर्यां चरन्तः ।
सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा ॥ ११ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tapaḥśraddhe ye hy upavasanty araṇye śāntā vidvāṃso bhaikṣacaryāṃ carantaḥ |
sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti yatrāmṛtaḥ sa puruṣo hy avyayātmā || 11 ||

lines.iast: tapaḥśraddhe ye hy upavasanty araṇye śāntā vidvāṃso bhaikṣacaryāṃ carantaḥ
lines.deva: तपःश्रद्धे ये ह्युपवसन्त्यरण्ये शान्ता विद्वांसो भैक्षचर्यां चरन्तः

lines.iast: sūryadvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti yatrāmṛtaḥ sa puruṣo hy avyayātmā
lines.deva: सूर्यद्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्रामृतः स पुरुषो ह्यव्ययात्मा

padaccheda.iast: tapaḥ-śraddhe ye hi upavasanti araṇye śāntāḥ vidvāṃsaḥ bhaikṣa-caryām carantaḥ sūrya-dvāreṇa te virajāḥ prayānti yatra amṛtaḥ saḥ puruṣaḥ hi avyaya-ātmā
padaccheda.deva: तपः-श्रद्धे ये हि उपवसन्ति अरण्ये शान्ताः विद्वांसः भैक्ष-चर्याम् चरन्तः सूर्य-द्वारेण ते विरजाः प्रयान्ति यत्र अमृतः सः पुरुषः हि अव्यय-आत्मा

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.
past active participle m. nom. pl.

words.meaning: by the door of the sun

translations.text: But those who practise austerity and faith in the forest, calm, learned, living on alms, go forth, free from stain, by the door of the sun to where that immortal Puruṣa (Hiraṇyagarbha), of undecaying nature, is.

notes: Śaṅkara: those with the opposite kind of knowledge, forest-dwellers and renouncers: tapas is the rite of their own stage of life, śraddhā the knowledge (meditation) whose object is Hiraṇyagarbha and the like; they live in the forest; śāntāḥ: with the senses withdrawn; vidvāṃsaḥ: householders too, given chiefly to knowledge; living on alms, having no possessions. sūryadvāreṇa: by the northern path, marked by the sun. virajāḥ: their merit and demerit exhausted. yatra: the world of satya and the rest, where that immortal Puruṣa is, the first-born Hiraṇyagarbha, undecaying, that is, lasting as long as the round of birth and death.

Śaṅkara, on the same: these are the farthest goals within the round, reached by the lower knowledge. Some hold this to be liberation; no, for the Upaniṣad says ‘here itself all desires dissolve’ (3.2.2) and ‘having reached the all-pervading everywhere … they enter the All’ (3.2.5); nor is liberation the topic here, where the lower knowledge is being treated. The freedom from stain is only relative. All that the lower knowledge brings about, the duality of means and ends divided into act, factors and fruit, ends with reaching Hiraṇyagarbha (Manu 12.50).

sanskrit.deva:
परीक्ष्य लोकान्कर्मचितान्ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन ।
तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत्समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम् ॥ १२ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
parīkṣya lokān karmacitān brāhmaṇo nirvedam āyān nāsty akṛtaḥ kṛtena |
tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurum evābhigacchet samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham || 12 ||

lines.iast: parīkṣya lokān karmacitān brāhmaṇo nirvedam āyān nāsty akṛtaḥ kṛtena
lines.deva: परीक्ष्य लोकान्कर्मचितान्ब्राह्मणो निर्वेदमायान्नास्त्यकृतः कृतेन

lines.iast: tadvijñānārthaṃ sa gurum evābhigacchet samitpāṇiḥ śrotriyaṃ brahmaniṣṭham
lines.deva: तद्विज्ञानार्थं स गुरुमेवाभिगच्छेत्समित्पाणिः श्रोत्रियं ब्रह्मनिष्ठम्

padaccheda.iast: parīkṣya lokān karma-citān brāhmaṇaḥ nirvedam āyāt na asti akṛtaḥ kṛtena tad-vijñāna-artham saḥ gurum eva abhigacchet samit-pāṇiḥ śrotriyam brahma-niṣṭham
padaccheda.deva: परीक्ष्य लोकान् कर्म-चितान् ब्राह्मणः निर्वेदम् आयात् न अस्ति अकृतः कृतेन तद्-विज्ञान-अर्थम् सः गुरुम् एव अभिगच्छेत् समित्-पाणिः श्रोत्रियम् ब्रह्म-निष्ठम्

translations.text: Having examined the worlds built up by action, a brāhmaṇa should come to dispassion: the unmade is not (won) by what is done. To know that, he should go, fuel in hand, to a teacher alone, one versed in the Veda and established in Brahman.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: now, to show who is fit for the higher knowledge, one who has turned away from the whole round of means and ends.

Śaṅkara: lokān: the worlds that are the fruit of the rites of the lower knowledge, which are enjoined only for one who has the natural faults of ignorance, desire and action, the worlds of the southern and northern paths, and the hells, animal births and ghostly states that come of neglecting what is enjoined and doing what is forbidden. Having examined them by perception, inference, comparison and scripture, and settled their nature on every side: from the unmanifest down to the plants, manifest and unmanifest, causing one another like seed and sprout, crowded with countless evils, pithless as the stem of a plantain, like illusion, a mirage, a city in the clouds, a dream, a bubble, foam, perishing every moment; built up by action prompted by ignorance and desire, made by dharma and adharma; having put them behind him. brāhmaṇaḥ: the brāhmaṇa is named because he especially is fit for the knowledge of Brahman by renouncing everything.

Śaṅkara, on the dispassion: nis with vid here means dispassion. Its form: in this round there is nothing at all that is unmade; all worlds are built by action, and so impermanent; nothing permanent exists here, and all action is a means only to what is impermanent, for all that action brings about is of four kinds, produced, reached, modified or purified; action has no further object. ‘I seek what is permanent, immortal, fearless, unchanging, unmoving, constant, not its opposite: what use is action, full of toil, a means of harm?’ So turned away, to know the fearless, auspicious, unmade, permanent state, he should go to a teacher alone, one endowed with calm, restraint and the rest; ‘alone’ means that even one learned in scripture should not seek the knowledge of Brahman on his own. samitpāṇiḥ: carrying a load of fuel. śrotriya: rich in study and in understanding what is heard. brahmaniṣṭha: one who, giving up all rites, rests in the one, non-dual Brahman alone, as one says ‘resting in japa, in austerity’; one engaged in rites cannot rest in Brahman, since action and knowledge of the Self are opposed. Having approached such a teacher in due form and won his favour, he should ask about the imperishable, true Puruṣa.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय सम्यक्प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय ।
येनाक्षरं पुरुषं वेद सत्यं प्रोवाच तां तत्त्वतो ब्रह्मविद्याम् ॥ १३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai sa vidvān upasannāya samyak praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya |
yenākṣaraṃ puruṣaṃ veda satyaṃ provāca tāṃ tattvato brahmavidyām || 13 ||

lines.iast: tasmai sa vidvān upasannāya samyak praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya
lines.deva: तस्मै स विद्वानुपसन्नाय सम्यक्प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय

lines.iast: yenākṣaraṃ puruṣaṃ veda satyaṃ provāca tāṃ tattvato brahmavidyām
lines.deva: येनाक्षरं पुरुषं वेद सत्यं प्रोवाच तां तत्त्वतो ब्रह्मविद्याम्

padaccheda.iast: tasmai saḥ vidvān upasannāya samyak praśānta-cittāya śama-anvitāya yena akṣaram puruṣam veda satyam provāca tām tattvataḥ brahma-vidyām
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै सः विद्वान् उपसन्नाय सम्यक् प्रशान्त-चित्ताय शम-अन्विताय येन अक्षरम् पुरुषम् वेद सत्यम् प्रोवाच ताम् तत्त्वतः ब्रह्म-विद्याम्

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. sg.
past passive participle m. dat. sg.

translations.text: To him who has approached rightly, whose mind is calm, who is endowed with calm (of the senses), the knowing one should teach in truth that knowledge of Brahman by which one knows the imperishable, the true Puruṣa.

notes: Śaṅkara: vidvān: the teacher who knows Brahman. samyak: as the scripture lays down. praśāntacitta: free of pride and the like; śamānvita: with the outer senses withdrawn, turned away from everything. puruṣa: so called because it is full (pūrṇa) and lies in the city (puri śayana) of the body; satya: being by nature the highest truth, undecaying; akṣara: because it does not flow away, is not hurt, does not waste. provāca stands for prabrūyāt, ‘should teach’: the rule binds the teacher too, to bring across the great ocean of ignorance a good pupil who has come to him as is right.
